place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 外门 · 伙房门口
place.en: Chending Temple · The outer court · outside the kitchen

setup.zh: 腊月初八，天没亮，伙房门口冻成了一面镜子。腊八粥熬上了，阿禾端着碗挤过来。
setup.en: The eighth of the twelfth month, before dawn; the ground outside the kitchen has frozen to a mirror. The Laba porridge is on, and Ahe squeezes in with her bowl.

recap.zh: 腊月初八，钱掌柜把你的「一赔一百」改成了「一赔一百五」。阿禾不上台，压了一页底册在你碗底下：卢方，使完金刃，要喘一口气；祁长松，只有四个字。看完，烧了。
recap.en: On the eighth of the twelfth month Money-Keeper Qian changed your "one to a hundred" to "one to a hundred and fifty". Ahe, staying off the stage, slipped a page of the old contest records under your bowl: Lu Fang needs a breath after a metal blade; Qi Changsong, just four words. Read, then burned.

en: The eighth of the twelfth month, before dawn.
A hundred and fifty to one.

story.zh:
腊月初八，天没亮。钱掌柜眯着眼睛看了看扶着墙晃过来的那一个，拿炭条把最底下那行「一赔一百」抹了，改成「一赔一百五」。有人问：「怎么又涨了？」钱掌柜拨了一下算盘：「站都站不稳的，再少一成。」

阿禾端着碗挤到他旁边。小满把一株紫须芝搁在她碗边，根上那团黑土里缠着几粒焦谷，跟她布里包着的那三粒一个样。阿禾看了一眼，什么也没问，收进了袖子里。小满道：「你上不上台？」阿禾道：「不上。亲传不上大比，师父的规矩。」阿禾也不看他，又道：「你那一颗，得自己上台去抢。」

她从怀里摸出小本子，撕下一页，压在他碗底下：「我不上台，眼睛闲着。」那一页上，一行一个名字，都写着怎么赢、怎么输。看到最后一行——祁长松——只有四个字，他抬起头来。阿禾面无表情：「看完烧了。」
story.en:
On the eighth of the twelfth month, before it was light. Shopkeeper Qian narrowed his eyes at the one swaying along the wall, and rubbed out the "a hundred to one" in the bottom line with his charcoal and wrote "a hundred and fifty to one." Someone asked: "Why's it gone up again?" Shopkeeper Qian clicked his abacus once: "Can't even stand up straight. That's another tenth off."

Ahe squeezed in beside him with her bowl. Xiaoman set a purple-whisker lingzhi by the edge of her bowl; in the clod of black earth round its roots were twined a few scorched grains, just like the three she kept wrapped in cloth. Ahe glanced at it, asked nothing, put it away in her sleeve. Xiaoman said: "Are you going up on the stage?" Ahe said: "No. Personal disciples don't enter the contest. Master's rule." Ahe didn't look at him either. She said: "Yours, you'll have to go up on the stage and grab for yourself."

She took her little notebook out of her robe, tore out a page and tucked it under his bowl: "I'm not going on the stage. My eyes have nothing to do." On that page there was one name to a line, each with how they won and how they lost. When he reached the last line, Qi Changsong, there were only four words, and he raised his head. Ahe was slurping porridge, her face blank: "Burn it when you've read it."

story_full.zh:
腊月初八，天没亮，小满趿着一双借来的破鞋从大通铺出来，腿还是软的。夜里下过一层冻雨，伙房门口那片空场冻成了一面镜子，排队打粥的人一个个扶着墙走。他也扶着墙，走一步，晃一晃。

钱掌柜裹着一床棉被，守在老槐树底下的押宝板跟前收早押。他眯着眼睛看了看扶着墙晃过来的那一个，看看他的腿，又看看他那张白得像纸的脸，拿炭条把最底下那行「一赔一百」抹了，改成「一赔一百五」。有人问：「怎么又涨了？」钱掌柜拨了一下算盘：「站都站不稳的，再少一成。」

伙房里的腊八粥早熬上了。米是陈米，豆是杂豆，枣子掰开来一只里头倒有半只是空的，可一大锅熬下来，热气腾腾，香得半座山都闻得见。小满排在队尾，脚底下还在打滑，手里端的是伙房大娘留给他的那一只没有缺口的碗。周衡也在排队，手里照例捏着那本账簿，回头看了一眼那锅粥，道：「年底了。账要结。」他把账簿拍了一拍，端着粥走了。

阿禾端着碗挤到他旁边。小满把一株紫须芝搁在她碗边，根上那团黑土里缠着几粒焦谷，跟她布里包着的那三粒一个样。阿禾看了一眼，什么也没问，收进了袖子里，吸溜了一口粥。小满道：「你上不上台？」阿禾道：「不上。亲传不上大比，师父的规矩。」小满道：「那颗筑基丹——」阿禾道：「不是给我的。师父说，我那一颗，到时候他自会给。」她说得很平，像说今天的粥稀。小满「哦」了一声，低头喝粥，碗里半只空枣，他嚼了很久。阿禾也不看他，又道：「你那一颗，得自己上台去抢。」

她从怀里摸出小本子，撕下一页，折成指甲盖大小，压在他碗底下：「我不上台，眼睛闲着。」这一个月，她跟着观主进内门坐过几回早课；藏经阁里历年大比的底册，谁使什么、怎么赢、怎么输，执事都记着，也是随她翻的。那一页上，一行一个名字，字小得像蚂蚁排队，十来个，一个一个，都写着怎么赢、怎么输；卢方那一行他看了两遍，秦雁那一行也看了两遍。看到最后一行——祁长松——只有四个字，他抬起头来。阿禾吸溜着粥，面无表情：「看完烧了。叫人瞧见亲传给外门的抄底细，师父的脸没处搁，我的也没处搁。」她的声音压得比粥还低。
story_full.en:
On the eighth of the twelfth month, before it was light, Xiaoman came out of the long bunk shuffling in a pair of borrowed worn-out shoes, his legs still weak. Freezing rain had fallen in the night, and the open ground outside the kitchen door had frozen into a mirror; the people queuing for porridge walked along the wall one by one, holding on. He held on to the wall too, swaying at every step.

Shopkeeper Qian, wrapped in a cotton quilt, was minding the betting board under the old pagoda tree, taking early bets. He narrowed his eyes at the one swaying along the wall, looked at his legs, looked at his face, white as paper, and rubbed out the "a hundred to one" in the bottom line with his charcoal and wrote "a hundred and fifty to one." Someone asked: "Why's it gone up again?" Shopkeeper Qian clicked his abacus once: "Can't even stand up straight. That's another tenth off."

The Laba porridge had been on in the kitchen for hours. The rice was old rice, the beans were mixed beans, and of the jujubes you broke open, one in two was half empty; but a whole great pot of it, steaming hot, smelled so good half the mountain could smell it. Xiaoman stood at the end of the queue, his feet still slipping, holding the one bowl without a chip that the kitchen woman kept for him. Zhou Heng was queuing too, the ledger in his hand as always. He looked back at the pot of porridge and said: "Year's end. The accounts have to close." He patted the ledger and went off with his porridge.

Ahe squeezed in beside him with her bowl. Xiaoman set a purple-whisker lingzhi by the edge of her bowl; in the clod of black earth round its roots were twined a few scorched grains, just like the three she kept wrapped in cloth. Ahe glanced at it, asked nothing, put it away in her sleeve, and slurped her porridge. Xiaoman said: "Are you going up on the stage?" Ahe said: "No. Personal disciples don't enter the contest. Master's rule." Xiaoman said: "That Foundation Pill—" Ahe said: "It isn't for me. Master says, mine, he'll give me himself when the time comes." She said it quite flatly, as if saying the porridge was thin today. Xiaoman said "Oh" and bent to his porridge; there was half an empty jujube in his bowl, and he chewed it for a long time. Ahe didn't look at him either. She said: "Yours, you'll have to go up on the stage and grab for yourself."

She took her little notebook out of her robe, tore out a page, folded it to the size of a fingernail and tucked it under his bowl: "I'm not going on the stage. My eyes have nothing to do." This month she had gone with the Abbot into the inner sect to sit at morning lessons a few times; the records of every year's contest in the Scripture Library (who used what, how they won, how they lost: the stewards wrote it all down) were hers to leaf through too. On that page there was one name to a line, the writing as small as ants in a queue, ten or so of them, each with how they won and how they lost. He read Lu Fang's line twice, and Qin Yan's line twice too. When he reached the last line, Qi Changsong, there were only four words, and he raised his head. Ahe was slurping porridge, her face blank: "Burn it when you've read it. If anyone sees a personal disciple copying out what's what for the outer sect, Master's face has nowhere to go, and mine has nowhere to go either." Her voice was pitched lower than the porridge.

exits.means: goes down to the contest stage on the training ground

refuse.zh: 阿禾那页纸还压在碗底下——看完，烧了。
refuse.en: Ahe's page is still under your bowl — read it, then burn it.

_beats: 古六 (2026-10-15): 底册 (laba-diche) stands at 「看完烧了」 — the page read and burnt at the 灶口; only the three lines the book gives are legible (卢方 古六, 秦雁 古七's notebook, 祁长松 「没法打，认输」), the rest stay ant-sized. Its mark `diche` lets him read 卢方 and 秦雁 (望气) at the 大比.
